div.head: Ps Cn for Prol
div.ab: He sunt sanctiones de foresta, quas ego Canutus rex, cum consilio primariorum hominum meorum de foresta, condo et facio, ut cunctis regni nostri Anglie ecclesiis et pax et iustitia fiat, et ut omnis delinquens rite secundum modum delicti et delinquentis fortunam patiatur.
div.note: New row (October 2026): Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 620 (two independent readings of the page images, differences settled against the page)
div.ab: These are the ordinances concerning the forest which I, King Cnut, with the counsel of my chief men, make and enact concerning the forest, so that both peace and justice may be done to all the churches of our realm of England, and so that every offender may duly suffer according to the manner of the offence and the fortune of the offender.
div.note: In Cn I 1; In Cn I 2.1; In Cn I 2.2

note.seg: Hæ Ho und oft æ und œ für e der anderen Hss., wohl humanistische Correctur
Hæ Ho, and often æ and œ for e of the other MSS, probably a humanist correction
forestarum St Cii
forestarum St Cii
diese Zufügung soll Cnuts Landrecht zum Forstrecht stempeln, auch 11. 13s. 14. 17e. 18
This addition is meant to stamp Cnut's general law as forest law; likewise 11, 13 n. s, 14, 17 n. e, 18.

auf regis arbitrio, .. uoluntaria principum institutione begründet das Forstrecht Dial. de scacc. I 11G (vgl. Edition Hughes p. 200); doch erwähnen Heinrichs II. und Richards I. Forstassisen die Beistimmung der Grossen

The Dialogus de scaccario I 11 G bases forest law on regis arbitrio, .. uoluntaria principum institutione (cf. Hughes's edition, p. 200); yet the forest assizes of Henry II and Richard I mention the assent of the magnates.
concilio Cii
concilio Cii

Verf. meint, laut des Zusatzes, nicht die Reichsmagnaten, sondern vielleicht die Oberförster in 1. Vgl. forestarum per comitatum Berkescire primas unter Heinrich I. (Chron. Abingdon. II 7), was aber kein Amtstitel ist, wie auch primores für die Constituenten des Grafschaftsgerichts (ebd. 120) nicht technisch lautet

To judge by the addition, the author means not the magnates of the realm but perhaps the chief foresters in 1. Cf. forestarum per comitatum Berkescire primas under Henry I (Chron. Abingdon. II 7), which however is not an official title, just as primores for the members of the shire court (ibid. 120) is not a technical term.

S. Gl Forst 6h. 15. a. Der Pluralis majestatis (s. d. Gl) im Pronomen possessivum begegnet häufig schon in Agsächs. Urkk. 9. Jhs.; weiter unten aber wird er auch sonst gebraucht

See Gl Forst 6h. 15. a. The plural of majesty (see that word in Gl) in the possessive pronoun occurs frequently already in Anglo-Saxon charters of the 9th century; further below, however, it is used elsewhere too
Verf. plant vielleicht ein forstliches Strafrecht gegen willkürliche Misericordia (s. d. Gl 7b) regis
The author is perhaps planning a forest penal law against arbitrary misericordia (see that word in Gl 7b) regis
